title: config/library keyword family: rejects a LEGAL config/library source with `NoModule` instead of proving reservedness
detail: The file is a well-formed A.1.1 `library_declaration` + `config_declaration`. §1.1 makes the whole of IEEE 1364-2005 part of Verilog-AMS and Annex C.16 (verified against /tmp/vams/annex-c-veriloga.txt:162-188) lists ONLY connect, connectmodule, connectrules, driver_update, endconnectrules, merged, net_resolution, resolvedto, split, wreal as not-used-by-Verilog-A — none of these nine. A conforming AMS compiler ACCEPTS this source and FAILS the fixture. The expectation `//! reject NoModule` is not a diagnostic code: `NoModule` is a VerA error enum (src/root.zig:106, raised at src/root.zig:404 when `p.file.modules.len == 0`), and it is what VerA actually returns here — the visible diagnostic is E0201 `construct is not in the supported subset: `library``. So the fixture asserts VerA's parser state, not an LRM rule. An analog-only tool that happily accepts `real config;` passes it. VERIFIED empirically: all 217 Table B.1 spellings were fed to `zig-out/bin/vera --lint` as `module kk; real <kw>; endmodule`. 215 produce E0208 ("expected an identifier: found <kw>"); only `assert` and `net_resolution` are accepted. So every rewrite below passes on the day it lands — no `//! xfail`. Also verified the parser RECOVERS: a module with `real buf; real nand; real xor;` emits three separate E0208 diagnostics, each naming its spelling, so one family file with one `//! reject <spelling>` line per keyword really does prove each keyword individually (the runner ANDs the lines, tests/torture.zig:625-660). Rewrite in place as an Annex B reservedness census over the same 9 keyword(s): one module, one declaration list, one `//! reject <spelling>` line each. Keep the file name and number so COVERAGE.md's family table still resolves. Add `//! lrm B`, drop the `// EXPECT: error -- normative syntax/restriction snapshot for this rule family.` footer, and delete the matching .expected-error.txt (item B23).

title: The prohibition half of "An escaped identifier shall not be treated as a keyword" is untested tree-wide
detail: Annex B para 1 sentence 2 is a `shall not`. The whole corpus tests only the permissive half (this chapter's 01_escaped_keyword.va, plus ch02_lexical/03_escaped_identifiers.va and ch02_lexical/26_escaped_keyword.va, all of which make an escaped keyword a VARIABLE). VERIFIED by grep: of the 313 `//! reject` fixtures in tests/fixtures/, exactly one contains a backslash (ch02_lexical/38_string_line_continuation_rejected.va) and it is about strings. So a compiler that strips the backslash before the keyword lookup — the single most common way to get §2.8.1 wrong — passes every fixture in the tree. VERIFIED VerA is already correct: `\module  m5;` → E0201 `construct is not in the supported subset: `module``, and `\analog  begin ... end` inside a module → E0205 `unsupported module item: found analog`. No xfail. Write the in-module form as the primary — it proves the rule inside a design unit rather than at file scope, where a stray identifier is rejected for boring reasons.

title: No fixture pairs the escaped-identifier rule with a reserved spelling: `\sin ` must be a legal port exactly where `sin` is not
detail: ch10_directives/17 and /27 prove a port named `sin` is an error under a VAMS keyword set; ch10_directives/26 proves it is legal under "1364-2001" with `CHECKX(V(sin,n), 0.5)`. The escaped complement — same port, same bias, backslash — is the sharpest single test of "an escaped identifier shall not be treated as a keyword", because it puts the two rules in direct opposition. VERIFIED it compiles today: a module with ports `\sin , n` lints clean. CORRECTION to the uncovered lens: it proposed `` `begin_keywords "VAMS-2023" ``. There is no such version string in LRM 10.6 (the list is 1364-1995 / 1364-2001 / 1364-2001-noconfig / 1364-2005 / VAMS-2.3 / VAMS-2.4), and VerA silently ACCEPTS the bogus string, so writing it would bake a second bug into the fixture. Use no directive at all — VerA's default set already reserves `sin` — or `VAMS-2.3` as ch10/27 does. want = 0.5 is exact (0.75 - 0.25, binary-exact), so CHECKX is right.
